title: Sheet Pan Sausage and Summer Vegetables

items: 2 red bell peppers, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 medium eggplant, peeled and cut into ¾-inch pieces
1 medium zucchini, cut into ¾-inch pieces
1 medium red onion, sliced ¼ inch thick
2 lb sweet Italian sausage links (about 8 links), left whole
1 (12-oz) package cherry tomatoes (about 2 cups), left whole

steps: Set oven racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven. Put 2 rimmed sheet pans on the racks and preheat the oven to 425°F with the pans inside.
In a large bowl, add the bell peppers, eggplant, zucchini and red onion. Pour the olive oil over them, then sprinkle with the Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Toss until every piece is coated.

Using oven mitts, pull out the hot pans and split the vegetables between them in a single layer. Tuck the sausages in among the vegetables, about 4 per pan. The vegetables should sizzle when they hit the pan.
Roast for 15 min. Take the pans out, toss the vegetables and turn the sausages, then scatter the cherry tomatoes over both pans. Return the pans to the oven, switching their rack positions.

Roast 15 to 20 min more, until the sausages are browned and register 160°F inside on an instant-read thermometer, the vegetables are tender with browned edges, and the tomatoes are blistered and starting to burst.
Drizzle the balsamic vinegar lightly over the sausage and vegetables on the pans. Move everything to a large platter, spooning the pan juices over the top.
Sprinkle with the basil. Serve hot with the crusty bread for soaking up the juices and the grainy mustard on the side.
tips: Hot Italian, chicken or turkey sausage all work; fully cooked sausage such as kielbasa only needs to heat through to 165°F, so check it early.
Chop the vegetables up to 1 day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge until you roast.
Keep the vegetables in a single layer with space between pieces so they brown instead of steam.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months; the vegetables soften after freezing. Reheat on a sheet pan at 400°F for 10 to 12 min, or in the microwave, until the sausage reaches 165°F.

assumptions: The recipe makes 4 to 6 servings, so the totals were divided by the middle value of 5.
All sausage fat and the olive oil are counted because the pan juices are spooned over the platter.
The crusty bread is assumed to be a 1 lb loaf of French-style bread, and all of it plus the mustard is included.
The 2 tsp of kosher salt is estimated at about 3,000 mg sodium total, between Diamond Crystal and Morton values.
Sausage sodium and fat vary by brand; values use typical USDA raw sweet Italian pork sausage, and balsamic is figured at 1.5 Tbsp.
